paragraphs.text: Rogelio Anzures Tapia participated in Meeting LZC-10-01 on 2010-03-14. Bruma del Cobre was linked to Meeting LZC-10-01 on 2010-03-14. Meeting LZC-10-01 occurred at Lázaro Cárdenas on 2010-03-14. Regional press reporting from the Pacific coast described a gathering of port contractors in Lázaro Cárdenas that local columnists linked to the new Manzanillo network. One columnist named Anzures, better known in the ports as El Portuario, as the host and wrote that the discussion concerned which trucking lanes would be assigned to which crew. The press account is unverified and relies on unnamed port sources.

Gilberto Tinoco Arzate participated in Meeting LZC-10-01 on 2010-03-14. Rogelio Anzures Tapia led Bruma del Cobre from 2010-03-14 until 2014-08-02. A second column identified Tinoco, called El Grúa, as the logistics figure who presented the lane assignments to the contractors. The same column characterized Anzures as the undisputed head of the arrangement from its first day. The columns did not name the contractors present and gave no detail on how the lanes were to be divided between the two ports. A third press item from the same week described Anzures as a port broker with no criminal record, which the reporting office notes is consistent with his public profile before the founding of the network.

This digest summarizes open press reporting and carries no classification beyond the public domain. The reporting office has not corroborated the press accounts through its own sources. Place names in this report refer to the municipality unless a crossing or port is specified. The individuals named in this report have appeared in prior reporting under different nicknames. Readers should note that regional columnists in this period frequently repeated each other and that two accounts may rest on a single original source.
